svg.aria-label: In a component-dense styled view under FlatLaf, most of a frame is Look-and-Feel painting that SwingTree wraps but cannot cache; SwingTree's own rendering is a small slice.
svg.text: One repaint of a heavily styled view. Bar length is the measured repaint time; the segments are shares of sampled on-EDT time.
Indicative rather than a controlled A/B — the two views differ in window size and component count.
SwingTree’s own style rendering and cache blits — 5–7 %
under a SwingTree-native Look-and-Feel — 122 components — 1.22 ms
no foreign border to delegate to, so nearly all of this is style engine — and most of it is cache blits
SwingTree paints on top of whatever Look-and-Feel you installed, and it faithfully delegates to that LaF’s own border and body painting. That delegation cannot be
cached: a third-party delegate may read any component property, any UIManager value, or its own mutable fields, and a cache key that missed one bit would not fail
loudly — it would show a stale border forever. So the honest reading is that the frame above is mostly not SwingTree’s to spend, and mostly not SwingTree’s to save.
